Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ajay Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ajay Singh, learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant-Kamil, seeking enlargement in Case Crime No. 276 of 2021, under Sections 376, 504, 506,
363, 342 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, registered at P.S. Jani, District Meerut.
3. This is the second bail application.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 05.04.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 48870 of 2021.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the new and fresh ground in the present second bail application is that the report from the forensic expert has come, in which he did not find any spermatozoa/seminal fluid either in the vaginal swab or on the clothes of the victim.
It is further submitted that rape was committed by the applicant is thus not corroborated.

It is further submitted that the doctor conducting the medical examination of the victim did not find any injury on her vagina and even while she was cross examined, she has not found any injury in internal and external parts.
It is further submitted that the victim, although was not declared hostile by the trial court, but at certain places in the statement, there are contradictions.
It is next submitted that the applicant is in jail since 21.08.2021 and, the trial has not yet concluded.
He further submitted that he may be enlarged on bail.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the first bail of the applicant has been rejected on merits.
It is submitted that the report of the forensic lab would not be decisive of the fact whether rape has been committed or not.
It is submitted that the trial is under process.
The victim has supported the prosecution case and has levelled allegation of rape against the applicant.
It is submitted that there is no fresh and new ground in the present bail application and as such the present bail application of the applicant be rejected.
6. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the first bail application of the applicant has been rejected vide order dated 05.04.2022.

The said order reads as under:-
"Heard Sri N.I. Jafri, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Nasira Adil, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ehtesham Akhtar, learned counsel for the first informant and Sri S.B. Maurya, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Kamil, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 227 of 2021, under Sections 376, 363, 342, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act registered at Police Station Jani, District Meerut.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is argued that although the applicant is named in the first information report and there is an allegation that he kidnapped the minor daughter of the first informant and the first informant during search came to know that his daughter was seen in the house of the applicant, he went there where he was abused, while going inside he found his daughter to be lying on the bed in a tied position and then he rescued her and she narrated the incident is false and incorrect.
It is argued that the entire prosecution case is a falsity.

It is totally improbable that the prosecutrix would have been taken to the house of the applicant, kept in a room and tied there and rape would have been committed on her where the entire family members including various ladies, children and other persons were present.
It is Kamil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139859859/

entities.text: Kamil vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 further argued while placing paragraph 21 & 22 of the affidavit that the applicant's father lodged a first information report against one Khalid who was going to be the father-in-law of the victim in which charge-sheet has been submitted.
The applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 23 and is in jail since 21.08.2021.
Per contra, learned counsel for the first informant and learned counsel for the State have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
It is argued that the applicant is named in the first information report and there are allegations against him.
The first informant saw the victim in the house of the applicant in a tied condition who then rescued her and then he was told of the incident.
The prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has corroborated the prosecution case of rape by the applicant on her.
It is further argued that as per the school records of U.P. Board of class 9th of the year 2020, the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 05.05.2005 and as such she was a minor girl.
It is argued that there is no reason for falsely implicating the applicant.
In so far as the story of rape against the applicant is concerned, the same is consistent throughout.
After having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that as per the school records, the prosecutrix is a minor girl.
There is an allegation against the applicant of committing rape upon the prosecutrix after kidnapping her.
She was found in the house of the applicant by her father in a tied condition and was then rescued by him.

The reason as enumerated in paragraph 21 &
22 for false implication is too far fetched and has nothing to do with the parties and the present case.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case for bail,
hence, the bail application is rejected."
7. The report of the forensic lab is not the decisive factor in a matter like this.
The victim, even in the trial, has supported the prosecution case.
As of now, there is no fresh and new ground in the present bail application.
8. The second bail application is accordingly, rejected.
